newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens sharply on rate cut hope.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens sharply on rate cut hope.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell sharply against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in active and very volatile trading on Thursday, dealers said.

"We saw high demand for the dollar today as investors expect the Bank of Israel will lower interest rates. The dollar and the basket were trading for the last few months at a very low level and everybody is afraid the dollar may rise sharply soon," said Israel Sapir at Bank Leumi.

Hopes that the Bank of Israel will make a significant reduction in short-term rates grew on Tuesday with the news of a low 0.4 percent rise in the September consumer price index. The central bank is due to announce interest rates for November at the end of October.
"Nobody wants to take any risk and when the shekel started falling in early trading the banks started buying dollars. Nobody wants to get stuck in a short position on the dollar," Sapir said.

"Trading was very active and volatile. In early trading the shekel started falling on high demand from the banking sector. When the dollar reached 3.2360 shekels the business sector started selling dollars and the dollar fell to 3.2180 shekels," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"Just before the end of the trading day the shekel started falling again for no evident reason in very active trading," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2350 against 3.2030 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6096 shekels against 3.5712 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8879 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8551 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.1041 shekels against 2.0790 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2400 shekels.
